evidence: Immortalized human myoblasts from individuals with FSHD and their UASb were obtained from the Senator Paul D. Wellstone Muscular Dystrophy Cooperative Research Center for FSHD at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (Worcester, MA, USA) and Dr Woodring E Wright at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center.
The collection of muscle biopsies, isolation of myoblast and purification, and molecular characterization of FSHD and UASb cells were originally described by Homma et al..
Proteomic studies in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) could offer new insight into disease mechanisms underpinned by post-transcriptional processes.
We measured the abundance of 4420 proteins and the turnover rate of 2324 proteins in each (n = 4) myoblast sample.
